description_en: Degutale, also called Digutale, is the tallest monument building in the Patan Darbār Square. It is located between Mūla Coka to the south and Keśavanārāyaṇa Coka to the north. The structure faces west and is located to the east of the main street of the Darbar Square alongside a series of temples. The temple is built upon the solid masonry core of the ground floor and can be accessed from the first floor. To reach it, one must climb the flight of stairs attached to the north wall and pass through a stone arch doorway built on the boundary wall. The central door and two windows on the ground floor of the west wall are not operable, and have a core wall some 20 cm deep behind them.A three-bayed colonnaded space to the east of the building leads to the open area known as Nāsala Coka. This colonnaded space has three rows of carved columns that support the upper masonry work. The first floor has small elongated spaces around the solid masonry core lit only by small latticed windows. On the second floor, a central three-bay window on the western wall is flanked by lattice windows on either side. Similarly, the eastern elevation contains a central louvered three bay window with two latticed windows on either side. A unique feature of this building is the slanting and projecting window that engirds the entire building on the third floor. The window is furnished with lattice screens and small central openings. The western side is entirely open in the form of a series of eleven windows. Above the windows, a flat balcony also encircles the building on the fourth floor. On this level, one can find a golden door with atoraṇaabove it leading from the western side of the building out to the veranda. The whole floor is furnished with small lattice windows. This floor houses the main sanctum of the Taleju, where Degutale is enshrined. Above this level, one reaches the overhanging roof supported by struts on all sides. The three tiers of this monument have a grand presence in the palace complex. The lower two roofs are roofed with traditionaljhĩgaṭītiles while the upper roof is covered in flat metal sheets. The main golden pinnacle is gilded, and four small pinnacles stand at each corner on a brass-clad base. ­­The pinnacle at the north-western corner has almost completely separated from the roof and appears ready to fall down at any time. A statue of a hovering Yoga Narendra Malla alongside a serpent, a bird, and his queens has been erected on a tall stone pillar facing the Taleju temple. This can be found to the west of the building.Degutale is the tutelary deity of Malla kings. The Licchavi kings kept their lineage deity Ṣaṣṭhīdevī in their palace. It seems that in the Malla period, Ṣaṣṭhīdevī was replaced by Degutale (Vajrācārya2033, 75).Devamālā Vaṃśāvalī(see inYogī2013, 55) states that Śivasiṃha Malla took the advice of Lambakarṇa Bhatta and established this temple in 1584 (NS 704). Other chronicles also suggest that Śivasiṃha Malla was the one to establish this temple. It seems likely, therefore, that the king really was responsible for its construction. However, the date that it was constructed is therefore unlikely to have been NS 704. In NS 704, King Purandara Siṃha was ruling over Lalitpur, as mentioned in a colophon ofDurgāsaptasatīdated NS 717. This source states that Śivasiṃha only began his rule in NS 718 (Śākya2008, 63).The temple's original appearance is unknown. In 1641 (NS 761), Śivasiṃha’s grandson Siddhinarasiṃha Malla reconstructed the temple as a five-storey building. In 1663 (NS 783) the temple was destroyed by a fire and later reconstructed with four tiers by Śrīnivāsa Malla. The temple then collapsed in the 1934 earthquake; by 1940 it had been reconstructed in its present form. The Patan Darbar area is considered a World Heritage Site, and this temple is part of the area. As such, the Department of Archaeology, Nepal has been taking care of its repair and maintenance.
description_ne: ललितपुर दरवार क्षेत्रमा रहेको केशवनारायण चोक र मूलचोकको बीचमा देगुतले मन्दिर रहेको छ । देगुतलेलाई 'दिगुतले' पनि भनिन्छ । देगुतले मल्ल राजाहरूका देगुद्य: (कुलदेवता) (lineage deity / ancestral deity) हुन् । लिच्छविकालमा षष्ठीदेवकुल भनी कुलदेवताको पूजा गरिन्थ्यो । राजदरवारभित्रै षष्ठीदेवीको मन्दिर हुन्थ्यो र लिच्छविकालको षष्ठीदेवकुलको ठाउँ मल्लकालमा देगुतले मन्दिरले लिएको देखिन्छ (Vajrācārya 2033, 75). देगुतलेको मन्दिरमा प्रवेश गर्न नासल चोकभित्र जाने ढोका भएर जानुपर्छ । देगुतले मन्दिरसँगै उत्तरतिर जोडिएर बनेको पर्खालमा ढुंगाको प्रवेशद्वार बनाइएको छ । प्रवेशद्वारको केन्द्रमा महिषासुरमर्दिनी लगायत अन्य देवीका मूर्तिहरू कुँदिएका छन् । उक्त ढोकाबाट छिरेपछि ढुंगाको अग्लो सिँढी बनाइएको छ । त्यो सिँढी चढेर भित्र छिरेपछि नासल चोक जाने र दिगुतले मन्दिरमा जाने बाटो देखिन्छ । प्रचलित मन्दिरका रचनाभन्दा अलि पृथक ढंगले यो मन्दिर बनाइएको छ । यो मन्दिर भएपनि अन्य मन्दिरमा जस्तो तल्लो भागमा तहतह गरी पेटी नबनाई आवासीय घर जस्तो शैलीमा बनाइएको छ । पश्चिमाभिमुख यो मन्दिर तीन तहको छानासहित आठ तलाको बनाइएको छ । तीन तहको छानामध्ये सबभन्दा माथिल्लो छानामा धातुको पाता राखिएको छ भने बाँकी दुई तहको छानामा झिंगटी राखिएको छ । सबभन्दा माथिल्लो छानामा सुनको मोलम्बा लगाइएको गजूर राखी चारै कुनामा एक-एकवटा साना गजूरहरू राखिएका छन् । ती चार साना गजूरमध्ये उत्तर-पश्चिममा रहेको गजूर आफ्नो स्थानबाट छुट्टिएर खस्ला जस्तो अवस्थामा छ । छानाहरू अड्याउन विविध देवीदेवता अंकित कलात्मक टुँडालहरू राखिएका छन् । मन्दिरको चौथो तलामा कौसी निकालिएको छ । कौसीको पश्चिमी मोहडामा सुनको मोलम्बा लगाइएको ढोका राखिएको छ । ढोकामाथि शिवलिंग अंकित धातुको तोरण राखिएको छ । ढोकाको दायाँबायाँ गोलझ्याल राखिएका छन् । मल्ल राजाहरूको कुलदेवता यही तलामा राखिएको छ । मन्दिरको तेस्रो तलामा चारैतिर क्वस्व:झ्या: (inclined window) राखिएको छ भने बीचमा तोरण सहितको सानो झ्याल राखिएको छ । मन्दिरको दोस्रो तलामा बीचमा गा:झ्या: (balconied window) राखी दायाँबायाँ एक-एकवटा तिकिझ्या: राखिएका छन् । पहिलो तलामा तीनवटा तिकिझ्या: राखिएका छन् । मन्दिरको भुइँतलामा बीचमा एउटा ढोका राखी दायाँबायाँ एक-एकवटा तिकिझ्या: राखिएका छन् । भुइँतलामा रहेको यस ढोकाको खासै प्रयोजन छैन ।यो मन्दिरको निर्माणबारे कुनै अभिलेख भेटिएको छैन । देवमाला वंशावलीमा नेसं ७०४ मा राजा शिवसिंह मल्लले लम्बकर्ण भट्टसँग सरसल्लाह गरी तन्त्रविधान अनुसार देगुतलेको मन्दिर स्थापना गरेको कुरा लेखिएको छ (Yogī 2013, 55). शिवसिंह मल्लले देगुतलेको मन्दिर स्थापना गरेको कुरा अन्य वंशावलीमा पनि लेखिएकाले यसमा सत्यता हुनसक्छ, तर मन्दिर स्थापना गरेको मिति नेसं ७०४ हुनैसक्दैन किनकि नेसं ७०४ मा ललितपुरमा पुरन्दरसिंहको शासन चलिरहेको थियो । नेसं ७१७ ज्येष्ठ शुक्ल १० कोसप्तसतीग्रन्थको पुष्पिकावाक्यमा राजाको रूपमा पुरन्दरसिंहको नाम उल्लेख गरिएको छ भने नेसं ७१८ देखि मात्र ललितपुरका शासकका रूपमा शिवसिंहको उल्लेख पाइन्छ (Śākya 2008, 63). शिवसिंहले पहिले मन्दिर बनाउँदा कस्तो थियो भन्ने बारे कुनै जानकारी पाइँदैन, पछि उनका नाति सिद्धिनरसिंह मल्लले नेसं ७६१ मा त्यसलाई पाँच तल्ले मन्दिर बनाएका थिए । नेसं ७८३ मा आगलागीमा ध्वस्त भएपछि श्रीनिवास मल्लले त्यसलाई चार तहको मात्र छाना बनाई पुनर्निर्माण गरेका थिए । विसं १९९० को भूकम्पले भत्किएपछि हालको अवस्थामा तीन तहको छाना बनाई पुनर्निर्माण गरिएको थियो । पाटन दरवार क्षेत्र विश्व सम्पदा सूचीमा समावेश भएपछि यो मन्दिर पनि उक्त दरवारक्षेत्रको अंश भएकाले यस मन्दिरको मर्मतसंभार गर्ने काम पुरातत्त्व विभाग अन्तर्गत स्मारक संरक्षण तथा दरबार हेरचाह कार्यालयबाट भइरहेको छ ।

historical_events.event_name: Erection of Statue in front of Degutale
historical_events.event_description: King Yognarendra Malla erected the stone pillar in front of Degutale. To show his devotion to the deity, he placed images of himself and his two wives on top of it.

The temple was levelled during the earthquake of 1934 (Rāṇā1992, 115). TheDevmalavaṃśāvalīstates that all the three stories of the temple collapsed and the image of the main deity was covered in rubble (Yogī2013, 55).

Prime minister Juddha Śamśera reconstructed the temple and consecrated the deity in 1938 (VS 1995 Jestha 11). He was honoured withsindurajātrāand welcomed with many decorated gates in Patan. Gambling was also allowed from 9.00 pm on that day.

historical_events.event_name: Construction of five storied temple for Degutale
historical_events.event_description: Śivasiṃha Malla established the temple. However, we do not know whether he only installed the deity or if he really constructed the temple. King Siddhinarasiṃha Malla is credited for changing the structure of the Degutale; he turned it into a five-storey temple and made an offering of a golden pinnacle and a flag. Various historical records disagree on the dates that these events took place. TheDevmalāvaṃśāvalīmentions that this occured on NS 787 Jestha 2 (see inYogī2013, 55), whileBhaṣāvaṃśāvalīstates that it was NS 767, on the second of the dark half of Jestha (see inLamsāl2023, 62). The inscription, however, provides NS 761 as the date when this event happened. The inscription appears to be the most authentic source.

Nepālikabhūpavaṃśāvalī(19.3.152) states that King Śrīnivāsa Malla rebuilt the three-tiered Degutale temple in NS 783. Aṭhyāsaphūrecording the historical events mentions that there was a huge fire on the sixth day of the bright half of Vaiśākha NS 783 (Regmi1966, part 3, page 100, Thyasaphu). A colophon ofKubjikāpaddhatimanuscript notes that Degutale was completely destroyed by the fire of NS 783 (Regmi1966, part 2, 76). Although the event year is similar, only one document provides the full date.
King Śrīnivāsa Malla offered the four pinnacles for the four corners of the Degutale.
